_comment: Shared cases for the two copies of test_src.rs (noo-cli/src and gateway-rust/src, followup 215). Both crates run every row and must produce exactly these outputs, so a change to one copy fails until the other matches. own_code is byte-exact (comments blanked to spaces, test-only items removed); each body is fn_body(of, marker); each stale marker must panic 'this guard is stale' on own_code.

cases.name: guard_fixture
cases.why: A doc comment naming the call, a test-only fn ABOVE the code under guard, a function followed by a test module, braces inside strings, raw strings, char literals and lifetimes.

cases.name: column_zero_brace_in_a_raw_string
cases.why: The first column-0 closing brace is inside a raw string, not the function's end.

cases.name: module_and_impl_markers
cases.why: A non-fn item is bounded the same way; fn_body over the raw source keeps a test module whole, own_code drops it.

cases.name: multibyte_text
cases.why: Non-ASCII in comments, strings and chars survives blanking, byte for byte.
cases.src:
fn f() { let _ = "—"; let c = 'é'; } // a — dash
/* ünïcode */ fn g() {}
cases.own_code:
fn f() { let _ = "—"; let c = 'é'; }              
                fn g() {}

cases.name: items_ending_in_a_semicolon
cases.why: A test-only use or const ends at its own semicolon (not one inside brackets); an attribute inside a string or a comment is not an item.
cases.own_code:
const NOTE: &str = "#[cfg(test)] is just text";
                            
fn kept() { let b = b"}"; let rb = br#"{"#; }

bodies.body: fn kept() { let b = b"}"; let rb = br#"{"#; }

cases.name: nested_block_comments_and_lifetimes
cases.why: Block comments nest; a lifetime is not a char literal, so the brace after it is code.

cases.name: raw_string_holding_a_quote_and_a_brace
cases.why: A raw string may hold a quote followed by a closing brace; read as an ordinary string, that brace would be code and end the body early.
